candidate.answerReason: The meetings total 135 minutes out of a 540-minute workday, which is 25%, agreeing with C.

methods.label: Find the meetings' share of the workday
methods.explanation:
Use the same time unit for the meetings and the whole workday. The second meeting lasted \(2\cdot45=90\) minutes, so the total meeting time was \(45+90=135\) minutes. The workday lasted \(9\cdot60=540\) minutes. Therefore the percentage spent in meetings was
\[
\frac{135}{540}\cdot100\%
=\frac14\cdot100\%
=\boxed{25\%},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only time-unit conversion, whole-number arithmetic, and a part-to-whole percentage are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is calculating a percentage rate from a part and a whole. Converting hours to minutes makes the quantities comparable, while percentage meaning and fraction-to-percent conversion support the calculation.
